Wagertech <> Jumpr: Weekly Sync

Invited Marc Cabantog lina@wagertech.bet Kobi Kunasekaran emily@wagertech.bet joyce@wagertech.bet Waleed Alasadi Taryn Reithofer strah@wagertech.bet strahinja.vladetic@gmail.com Miko Sumagang

Attachments Wagertech <> Jumpr: Weekly Sync

Meeting records Transcript Recording 

Summary

The team defined integration protocols, structured brand ambassador records, and established standardized player and referrer statuses.

System Integration and Testing
Testing utilizes live data to prioritize volume analysis while shifting deduplication logic to a person account model. The group decided to implement API keys and IP whitelisting for integration security.

Ambassador Data Model Design
Reporting structures depend on standard manager fields, and unnecessary data fields like verticals are removed to streamline records. Standardized ambassador statuses facilitate consistent operational reviews.

Status and Referral Definitions
Player and referrer statuses trigger internal flagging after 90 days of inactivity. Referral records reside exclusively within the sales platform to maintain data integrity.

Decisions

Aligned

  • Sandbox data designated as throwaway The team designates all data pushed to the sandbox environment as throwaway data for the duration of the API testing phase.
  • Salesforce deduplication logic disabled The Salesforce integration will refrain from implementing internal deduplication logic, relying instead on the source system to send clean, deduplicated data for processing.
  • Test deals effective start date All test deals are effectively activated as of today's date for the purpose of integration testing.
  • Unconfigured agent data handling Incoming data for agents not yet configured in the system will be flagged for review rather than creating signup records.
  • API integration launch target The go-live target for initial API integration testing is scheduled for Thursday.
  • Slack-based error notification implementation A Slack connector will be implemented to provide real-time visibility into errors surfacing from the queue.
  • CMS-side API endpoint architecture Integration architecture is set to build an API endpoint on the CMS side for Salesforce to call, rather than establishing a Salesforce-initiated connection.
  • API endpoint security configuration The API endpoint security strategy is finalized as IP whitelisting combined with API keys.
  • Manual Salesforce rep administration Rep account creation and permission management will be conducted as a manual administrative task in Salesforce rather than via automated CMS integration.
  • Brand Ambassador status definitions Brand Ambassador status definitions are set to: active, paused, inactive, and terminated.
  • Standard Salesforce hierarchy adoption The standard Salesforce out-of-the-box manager field and user hierarchy will be utilized for managing Brand Ambassador and Manager relationships.
  • Secondary market tracking method Secondary market tracking will utilize multi-select picklists to accommodate multiple market assignments per Brand Ambassador.
  • Automation added for termination tracking The system will include an automation to track the termination date for users.
  • Unnecessary BA fields removed The 'payment method', 'preferred contact method', and 'payment frequency' fields will be removed from the Brand Ambassador records.
  • Login and contact email fields separated Separate fields will be created for the login username, primary email, and transfer email to ensure distinct data storage.
  • Verticals field removed The 'verticals' field will be removed from the Brand Ambassador record.
  • Landing page field renamed The 'landing page' field will be renamed to 'agency site' and retained alongside slug and external ID fields.
  • Copy functionality excluded from launch Custom copy-paste functionality will not be implemented for launch, relying on standard text selection instead.
  • Player currency defaulting logic established Player record currency will default to the currency of the first associated signup.
  • Manual VIP toggle implemented A manual VIP toggle restricted to authorized users will be implemented for player records.
  • BA attribution mismatch flagging implemented Signups and Clicks (SLC) where the assigned BA does not match the player's BA will be flagged for manual Ops review.
  • Survey completion field removed The 'survey completion' field will be removed from the record.
  • Player inactive status threshold set Player inactive status will trigger automatically after 90 days of inactivity.
  • Banned player status visual indicator Banned player status will be indicated via a top-level banner rather than specific restriction fields.
  • Referrer inactive status threshold set Referrer inactive status will trigger automatically after 6 months of inactivity.
  • Flagging strategy for restricted referrers Signups from paused or banned referrers will not be blocked, but flagged for Ops review.
  • Payout preference moved to notes The 'payout preference' field will be moved to a general notes section at the bottom of the record.
  • Email-based referrer deduplication Email-based deduplication will be implemented for referrers, blocking the creation of duplicate records.

Shelved

  • Storage proofs development shelved The development of storage proofs is deprioritized and shelved in favor of focusing on deal configuration tasks.
  • Prevel status field removed The 'Prevel status' field will not be included in the current development scope.

We've updated the Decisions section using your feedback.

Next steps

  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Setup Salesforce Deals: Configure all deal and deal assignment records within the Salesforce environment.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Share Deal IDs: Provide the generated identifiers for deals and assignments to the technical team for ingestion.
  • [Strahinja Vladetic] Build API Endpoint: Create a communication endpoint on the CMS to receive data transfers from Salesforce.
  • [Joyce Kiddell] Update Slack Notifications: Add the relevant team member to the existing error reporting channel to ensure visibility.
  • [Strahinja Vladetic] Enhance API Logging: Review and improve the current logging mechanisms to ensure error tracking is robust.
  • [Emily Vandenberg] Validate Live Data: Monitor the signup data flows following the production release to ensure accuracy.
  • [The group] Update Workflow Spec: Modify the specification documentation for the workflow between account creation in Salesforce and the Content Management System.
  • [Strahinja Vladetic] Set Up Endpoint: Establish the API endpoint and provide necessary details for record creation based on the shared specifications.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Update Integration Documentation: Refine the main Content Management System integration document with updated payload information once configured.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Update API Docs: Amend the initial API documentation using the latest design specifications and data requirements.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Evaluate Record Customization: Determine the feasibility of using out of the box Salesforce user records versus custom objects to track Brand Ambassador information.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Verify Copy Functionality: Investigate the implementation complexity for adding a copy to clipboard feature for specific fields on player records.
  • [Emily, Joyce] Clarify VIP Process: Determine the specific workflow and requirements for the VIP stream to ensure correct implementation.
  • [Kobi] Review BA Customization: Assess the customization capabilities for the Brand Ambassador page and provide an update on the findings.
  • [Kobi] Update Screen Layouts: Configure the fields, placement, and layouts for all specified Salesforce screens by next Monday.
  • [Joyce] Review Salesforce Screens: Review the updated screen layouts and provide feedback on the configurations.
  • [The group] Screen Review Meeting: Conduct a comprehensive end to end review of every Salesforce screen next Monday.

Details

Did the screenshots in this section make your notes better or worse?

  • Sandbox and API Testing: Emily Vandenberg and Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that all data pushed into the sandbox environment for API testing regarding study link clicks should be treated as throwaway data (00:00:56). The team agreed to proceed with testing using live data to observe volume and identify potential errors, with the option to preserve specific records if necessary for production migration later (00:03:36).
  • Player and Person Account Deduplication Logic: The team discussed shifting from using player IDs—which effectively functioned as account IDs—to a "person account" logic to resolve issues with duplicated data across agency sites (00:02:41). Strahinja Vladetic noted that while they will attempt to deduplicate records into a single "person" account on their side before sending data, the API will continue to support matching by email address as a fallback if the ID is unavailable (00:05:30). The team agreed to avoid implementing separate deduplication logic on the Salesforce side to prevent conflicts (00:07:25).
  • Historical Data Migration and Updates: Strahinja Vladetic explained the plan to perform an initial migration of historical data to roll up current duplicates into single person records, after which new logic in agency sites will prevent future duplication (00:06:24). Kobi Kunasekaran noted that while email address changes might be required in the future, the team will address this as needed, utilizing the existing API endpoint used for survey completion updates (00:07:25).
  • Technical Alignment and Integration Details: Emily Vandenberg and Strahinja Vladetic discussed the integration of operator and partner IDs into the CMS. Strahinja Vladetic confirmed that the provided Google Sheet contained the necessary IDs for Salesforce, and the team established a timeline to enable testing by the end of the next day (00:09:20).
  • Active Deal Setup: The team agreed to set the start date for active deals to the current date for testing purposes (00:11:23). Kobi Kunasekaran will configure the deals and deal assignments in Salesforce using external IDs, and Emily Vandenberg noted that future deals involving different agents will be handled by unlocking features at the slug level (00:12:23).
  • Sign-up Attribution and Rep Assignments: Kobi Kunasekaran explained that clicks will be mapped against specific deal IDs and deal rep assignments to allocate signups correctly (00:13:22). If rep assignments change or new reps are added, these updates will be made in Salesforce to ensure continued accurate attribution (00:14:32).
  • Testing and Monitoring Strategy: The team set a goal to go live with testing by Thursday. Kobi Kunasekaran and Emily Vandenberg will monitor the data flow, comparing CMS records against Salesforce to identify any errors (00:16:39). To ensure real-time visibility, the team discussed setting up a Slack connector to surface errors from the PubSub queue, which Strahinja Vladetic will implement (00:17:40).
  • Communication Link Between Salesforce and CMS: The participants discussed the need for a two-way communication link between Salesforce and the CMS (00:20:49). Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that an endpoint on the CMS side would be the standard approach, where Salesforce would push data or receive confirmation once deals are created or updated (00:22:05).
  • API Authentication and Security: Regarding the security of the API endpoint, the team agreed to utilize API keys and IP whitelisting as a secure and practical solution for their internal integration (00:26:19). Strahinja Vladetic will maintain the endpoint as public for the initial testing phase and introduce authentication layers afterward (00:29:09).
  • Future Integration Phases: The team decided to prioritize the current deal and rep assignment testing over storage proofs, which will be addressed in a future phase (00:29:09). Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that Cedric will shift focus to the current work instead of storage proofs for the time being (00:31:12).
  • Rep Management Workflow: The team clarified that adding new reps requires an administrative task in Salesforce to create user records and assign permissions, which cannot be fully automated through the CMS (00:33:24). Once a rep is created in Salesforce, the CMS will send the unique ID to match them, and any rep creation workflow will be documented and updated in the main integration specification (00:34:29).
  • Deal and Link Object Mockups: Joyce Kiddell presented mockups for deal and link objects, confirming that links will be objects appearing under deal details (00:41:39). The team agreed that link codes do not need to be unique for now, and discussed an "assignment cap" feature to prevent over-allocation of reps to specific links (00:42:54).

  • Brand Ambassador Statuses: The team reviewed status options for brand ambassadors, agreeing to use "Active," "Paused," "Inactive," and "Terminated" (00:47:53). Lina Ceniccola confirmed that the "Review" status is redundant if "Paused" is used, and "Terminated" will involve deactivating the user in Salesforce (00:49:11).

  • Brand Ambassador Record Structure: Kobi Kunasekaran advised that because Salesforce user records have limited customization for visual layouts, they will likely create a separate custom object linked to the user record to display rollups and related lists (00:51:28). If this proves too complex, the team agreed that using reports to surface data based on ownership is an acceptable alternative (00:52:27).
  • Hierarchy and Market Reporting: The team agreed to use the standard "manager" field in Salesforce to handle hierarchies, allowing managers to see signups for their subordinates (00:54:07). Joyce Kiddell and Kobi Kunasekaran discussed tracking primary and secondary markets for brand ambassadors, with the team planning to utilize multi-picklists for reporting purposes (00:57:24).
  • Reporting Data Grouping: Kobi Kunasekaran recommended avoiding multi-lists in reports because grouping by secondary markets can cause issues, such as creating separate entries for the same user; the group agreed to remove this for current reporting purposes (00:58:46).
  • User Record Fields: Joyce Kiddell and Kobi Kunasekaran discussed tracking start dates, with Kobi Kunasekaran suggesting the addition of an automation to track termination dates automatically (00:58:46). They agreed to keep primary email and e-transfer email fields separate (00:59:51).
  • Contact and Payment Methods: The team decided to update the contact method dropdown to include WhatsApp, email, text, and phone call while removing Slack (00:59:51). They further agreed to remove "check" as a payment option and concluded that payment frequency and specific contact methods could be managed within payroll or removed from the record to avoid unnecessary data entry (01:00:51).
  • System Field Strategy: Emily Vandenberg and Kobi Kunasekaran agreed to avoid flooding the system with unnecessary fields, opting to defer the addition of specific payout-related inputs until they are needed for the payout module scope (01:02:16).
  • Currency and Login Credentials: Lina Ceniccola and Joyce Kiddell agreed to keep the currency field, while Kobi Kunasekaran noted that if a login email differs from a primary email, they would create distinct fields for both (01:03:08).
  • Brand Ambassador Verticals: Joyce Kiddell, Lina Ceniccola, and Emily Vandenberg discussed the "verticals" field under brand ambassador details and decided to remove it as it was a roll-up and not required for specific assignments (01:04:26).
  • CMS Data Details: The group agreed to include an external ID, a slug, and a landing page field, with the latter renamed to "agency site" to improve clarity (01:05:35).
  • Copy Functionality: Joyce Kiddell and Emily Vandenberg explored adding a copy feature for BA details, but Kobi Kunasekaran explained that an out-of-the-box solution does not exist. Lina Ceniccola decided to keep the interface simple and rely on standard text selection for now rather than building a custom component (01:06:34).
  • Player Signup Currency: Kobi Kunasekaran clarified that while the system requires a currency value for every record, it can be defaulted based on the country or the first signup; the team confirmed that automated referral record creation is not currently planned (01:09:40).
  • VIP Identification: The team discussed how to mark players as VIPs, deciding on a manual toggle for the time being. Lina Ceniccola noted that approximately 30 manual records are processed per month, confirming this is a manageable volume for manual entry (01:11:47) (01:15:25).

  • Attribution and Fraud Review: Joyce Kiddell and Kobi Kunasekaran discussed reassigning BAs or players. Kobi Kunasekaran proposed that if an assigned BA does not match the record, the system should flag the signup for an operations review, allowing the team to correct errors or mark them as fraud without blocking the process (01:16:40).
  • Referral Documentation and Surveys: Joyce Kiddell clarified that referral information is added after a signup is logged, and the group agreed to remove the survey completion tracking object from the current scope (01:20:53).
  • Player Status Definitions: The team defined player statuses as pending, active, inactive, and banned, agreeing that an "inactive" status would be triggered by 90 days of no activity (01:23:07).
  • Banned Player Management: The group confirmed that the banned status is set manually and serves as a signal for internal review rather than a hard block on signups. This allows representatives to see if a banned player is attempting to sign up, facilitating fraud detection (01:26:54).
  • Referrer Statuses: The team defined referrer statuses as active, inactive (after six months), paused, and banned. They agreed that paused or banned statuses should serve as signals for operational review rather than system-wide restrictions on the referrer (01:29:13) (01:33:32).
  • Referrer Cleanup and Details: Joyce Kiddell and the team agreed to remove the referral "RO" field, keep country/state/province information, and rename the secondary contact field to "transfer email" (01:36:29) (01:38:46). They confirmed that referrer records will live entirely within Salesforce and will not sync with the CMS (01:40:02).
  • Access and Deduplication: Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that BAs should only see their own referrers unless they are a manager. They also discussed implementing email-based deduplication to prevent duplicate entries and explored creating a button to convert existing players into referrers via a screen flow (01:40:02).
  • Project Timeline: Kobi Kunasekaran estimated that page layouts and field updates would be completed by next Monday, and the team planned to perform an end-to-end review of all screens at that time (01:45:43) (01:47:25).
